item.title: What Kirby Smart said about Glenn Schumann's FSU football interest
item.description: Kirby Smart provided a brief comment on the future of No. 1 Georgia's defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann and his potential future as Florida State football's head coach. Speaking during a Monday, Nov. 23 press conference, the Georgia head coach was asked directly if he's had any conversations with Schumann about his potential move to take over as head coach of the Seminoles (5-6, 3-5 ACC). His response was brief. "Schumann has done a fabulous job here, and anything that comes from his success; he has earned every bit of it," Smart said. "But the University of Georgia is focused on Georgia Tech ." Short and sweet from Smart. But despite his avoidance, Schumann remains the Seminoles' frontrunner for the vacant head coach role, which became available after Mike Norvell was fired Nov. 1 . The university and Schumann have met to discuss the role, and multiple reports suggest that the two parties are close to an agreement. He has emerged as the lead candidate early in the Seminoles search, and his connection with now FSU athletic director Jeff Purinton could be playing a key role. Schumann and Purinton crossed paths at Alabama when Schumann started working as an undergraduate assistant under Nick Saban before he eventually followed Smart to Georgia. Schumann has earned a reputation for being an elite recruiter and developer of talent with the Bulldogs. One such example of that is linebacker Justin Williams. The former 5-star prospect who Schumann recruited to Athens spoke about the potential departure of his defensive coordinator when asked. "I know nothing about it. I mean, I’m really happy for him, whatever he chooses to do. He’s a great coach, great individual,” Williams said. "I see him like a father figure to me. He’s a great guy. So whatever he wants to do, I’m happy for him.” No public announcements have been made about the future of Schumann, but he remains the frontrunner in the Seminoles search ahead of a rivalry weekend for both teams. FSU hosts Florida, and Georgia faces Georgia Tech, meaning any offcial annoucments would likely be made after the pair of games. item.title: Viral video shows Denver looking silly on Josh Giddey’s game-tying layup – but it was all part of the plan
item.description: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Viral video shows Denver looking silly on Josh Giddey’s game-tying layup – but it was all part of the plan appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Denver Nuggets found themselves at the center of an unusual late-game sequence during their matchup with the Chicago Bulls . A viral clip showed Josh Giddey walking into an uncontested layup to tie the score in the closing seconds of regulation, making Denver’s defense look completely lost. However, the decision behind the play was more deliberate than it initially appeared. According to The Denver Post reporter Bennett Durando, Nikola Jokić believed he was fouled before committing the turnover that led to Chicago’s basket, a concern the coaching staff shared after reviewing the footage. However, Denver’s defensive approach on the other end was intentional. Cam Johnson explained that the Nuggets would rather concede an open two-point shot than allow Buddy Hield to get a clean three-pointer. “Buddy had it going, so we did not want him to finish the game with a 3. An open one,” Johnson said. JOKIC SENDS THE GAME TO OVERTIME 🔥 pic.twitter.com/okzh23tR1t Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) November 23, 2026 The sequence unfolded after Denver lost possession late in the fourth quarter. Chicago capitalized on the turnover, moving the ball to Giddey for an easy basket with 2.1 seconds remaining. The layup sent the game into overtime at 131-131, despite the Nuggets initially appearing to have control. Rather than risk giving Hield another opportunity from beyond the arc, Denver prioritized taking away his shot, even if that meant leaving the basket exposed. The strategy ultimately worked in the bigger picture, as the Nuggets recovered and pulled away in overtime. Denver outscored the Bulls in the extra period to secure a 151-145 road victory. Josh Giddey still delivered a remarkable performance in the loss, finishing with 23 points, 14 rebounds and 22 assists. His historic night made the viral defensive sequence even more memorable, but the Nuggets left Chicago with the win. item.description: The New York Giants pulled off the upset, defeating the talented Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, 23-18. Jacksonville was wildly undisciplined in the game; they committed 13 penalties for 107 yards, while out-gaining the Giants by 116 yards. The Giants, though, found a way to finish the pesky Jaguars, who hung around for far too long in the game. It was Dennard Wilson’s defense that harassed Trevor Lawrence and dictated to Liam Coen’s high-powered offense. Jacksonville mounted a comeback, with their final two drives totaling 135 of their total 354 yards. Coen, however, opted for a field goal with 3:40 left in the game on a fourth-and-goal at the Giants’ eight-yard line. The Jaguars were down by eight, and that decision cut the score to five points, but the Giants’ offense — who struggled for much of the game — secured a valuable first down that allowed New York to just run the clock out. item.title: How Geno Auriemma and Dawn Staley's rivalry evolved over 30 years
item.description: STORRS — When Geno Auriemma and Dawn Staley share the court on Tuesday night , the focus will be on two of women’s basketball’s most storied programs. But the relationship between the Hall of Fame coaches stretches back much longer than UConn and South Carolina, beginning when Staley was the star point guard for Virginia over 30 years ago. Since then, their relationship has evolved through the two programs’ dynastic runs and reached an uncomfortable flashpoint after last year’s Final Four confrontation. UConn vs South Carolina preview: Geno Auriemma downplays Dawn Staley subplot ahead of UConn-South Carolina showdown On Sunday , Auriemma said he would prefer the attention stay on the players. “I'm just trying to coach my team because they're the ones playing, and that's what people are coming to watch,” Auriemma said on Sunday. “I think they're coming to watch South Carolina and Connecticut play against each other.” With both teams meeting for the first time since last year’s Final Four, here’s a look at the timeline of Auriemma and Staley’s relationship. Player vs. Coach Staley has been on Auriemma’s radar since she was a kid. Back in 2016, Auriemma told ESPN that he first heard about Staley when she was a basketball prodigy in Virginia. "It's like she was the original Mo'ne Davis," Auriemma said. "From the time Dawn was in seventh or eighth grade, that's all anybody was talking about in girls' basketball. She had a reputation that preceded her when she got to Virginia [in 1988], and she was part of their greatest successes as a team.” Staley went on to play at Virginia from 1988 to 1992, coinciding with Auriemma’s first few years at UConn. Staley went 2-0 in her playing career against Auriemma, helping Virginia beat UConn in the 1991 Final Four and in a nonconference matchup during the 1991-1992 season. South Carolina’s rise Staley got her start in coaching in 2000 at Temple while she was still an active WNBA player. “I was still playing in the WNBA, but I was drawn to the difficulties and opportunities of turning a struggling basketball program around,” Staley wrote in the Players’ Tribune in 2015. Staley retired from playing in 2006 after 12 years of professional basketball. She left Temple two years later to coach at South Carolina. By then, Auriemma had led UConn to five national championships and nine Final Four appearances. Over the next decade, UConn established itself as the country’s premier women’s basketball program. But even as UConn cemented itself as the sport's dominant program, Staley was building South Carolina into a powerhouse. She won national championships in 2017, 2022 and 2024 and has guided the Gamecocks to eight Final Four appearances. “The trajectory that they've made has been very similar (to us),” Auriemma said on Sunday. “It's just harder now. item.title: Rams dealt another season-ending news before Packers game
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams are preparing for a difficult stretch of their NFL schedule as injuries continue to affect their roster. Head coach Sean McVay has already faced several selection problems, particularly on offense, where the team has lost important contributors. The Rams hoped to get some injured players back after their Week 11 bye. However, those plans have not gone as expected, leaving the coaching staff with more decisions to make before Wednesday’s meeting with the Green Bay Packers. The latest setback involves a young tight end who has spent much of the season recovering from an ankle injury. His situation has now taken another disappointing turn, with his return plans effectively coming to an end. MORE: Bhayshul Tuten injury update casts doubt on Jaguars RB’s Week 12 status Terrance Ferguson ruled out for remainder of season after Rams injury setback Los Angeles Rams tight end Terrance Ferguson (18) Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The Los Angeles Rams will not activate tight end Terrance Ferguson from injured reserve, according to ESPN’s Sarah Barshop. The reporter revealed on Monday, November 23, that Ferguson is still dealing with an ankle injury and will not return this season. Ferguson had been working toward a return after the Rams opened his 21-day practice window earlier in November. However, he suffered a hamstring injury during practice ahead of the team’s Week 9 game against the Washington Commanders. That setback delayed his comeback and kept him out of the lineup. Rams TE Terrance Ferguson is still dealing with an ankle and will not come off IR. He is done for the season. — Sarah Barshop (@sarahbarshop) November 23, 2026 McVay had previously indicated that the Rams planned to activate Ferguson before his practice window closed on November 25. The intention was to keep him on the active roster while he continued his recovery. Barshop’s latest update confirms that the situation has changed, ending his hopes of returning this season. Los Angeles Rams face tight end shortage before Packers matchup Ferguson’s absence creates another problem for the Rams as they prepare for Green Bay. The rookie has been unavailable since injuring his ankle earlier in the season, limiting the team’s options at tight end. Before his injuries, Ferguson had shown promise as a receiving option. He recorded seven catches for 63 yards and a touchdown across his first three games. His absence has left Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen to handle the position. The Rams will now need their remaining tight ends to contribute against the Packers on Wednesday, November 25. item.title: Max Verstappen jokes last time he won a race like F1 Las Vegas GP it was "Mario Kart"
item.description: Motorsport photo Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen says the last time he won a race like the Las Vegas Grand Prix was when he was playing Mario Kart . The Red Bull driver converted pole position into his 75th grand prix win, and his third in Las Vegas, in a race that featured 352 overtakes and 35 lead changes. Asked during the post-race press conference when he had last won a race like it, the Dutchman was reluctant to answer at first: "I probably shouldn't say it. I probably should not. I remember winning one like this when I was playing Mario Kart . "Sometimes you drop back and you get drafts, and there's like a catch-up, you know? Always when you're dropping back, you go faster. So that's the last time that I felt something like this," he said. The Red Bull driver was passed for the lead time and again, mostly by Mercedes' George Russell , and hit back every time. While he managed to retake the lead, he was not able to extend his advantage and break away from the pack behind him. "It was just the tow combination with the deployment. Of course, when you are within a second, you have the overtake mode as well, and around here that is powerful. So, yeah, you could not pull away." Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Asked whether he had enjoyed the race around the streets of Las Vegas, Verstappen drew a line between the driver and the spectator. "When I look at it from my racer heart, no. When you look at it as a show, spectacle, yes. I've enjoyed my repassing and everything, but I prefer to look at it with my racing heart." The race barely raised his pulse. "Even my heart rate, I was not nervous at all because, I don't know, it just felt kind of cruising out there, just trying to press the battery whenever it was correct or defend. But for the show, when you look at it from the outside, probably yes, you like it." Verstappen currently sits second in the drivers' standings. Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli claimed the title at the Mexican Grand Prix but the fight for second will continue into the upcoming Qatar Grand Prix. Verstappen has a 37-point lead over Lewis Hamilton , who sits third. George Russell and Lando Norris are fourth and fifth, respectively, both on 264 points. item.title: Syracuse football: QB Steve Angeli out, Malachi Nelson starts vs Notre Dame
item.description: CHESTNUT HILL, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 21: Steve Angeli #9 of the Syracuse Orange throws the ball against the Boston College Eagles during the first half at Alumni Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts. (Photo by Brian Fluharty/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Syracuse Orange will be without its starting quarterback against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish this Saturday. Syracuse Head Coach Fran Brown announced during his weekly press conference on Monday that Quarterback Steve Angeli will not play against the Fighting Irish. The Daily Orange’s Noah Nussbaum reported that Angeli had an AC joint injury. On3’s Pete Nakos reported that x-rays and imaging came back negative and that he could return for a bowl game. Quarterback Malachi Nelson will start his third game for the Orange this season. Angeli was injured after he took a sack towards the end of the first half against the Boston College Eagles in Syracuse’s last game. He was seen on the sideline with a sling. This will be the third game that Angeli has missed due to injury. He got a Plasma-Rich Platelet (PRP) shot earlier this year to his ankle and was sideline for Syracuse’s losses to Virginia and Louisville. This also means that Angeli will not get a chance to play his former team for the second year in a row. Angeli transferred to Syracuse from Notre Dame. He played in 21 games for the Fighting Irish, starting one game for the team. He started against Oregon State in the Sun Bowl in 2023, throwing for 232 yards and three touchdowns in that game. Angeli missed the Notre Dame game last year as he was still recovering from his Achilles surgery. The game saw the Orange give up 70 points for the first time in over 100 years. A late touchdown by Quarterback Joseph Filardi stopped the shutout but Syracuse still lost 70-7 in South Bend. Syracuse turns to Nelson for his third start in an Orange uniform. He started the games against Virginia and Louisville, which Angeli and quarterback Amari Odom were unavailable for. In those two games, Nelson threw for 532 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions on 42-68 passing. Nelson came into the Boston College game for Angeli after his injury. Nelson threw for 202 yards and a touchdown on 12-26 passing. He didn’t complete the game as he wasn’t available for the last drive due to injury. Quarterback Rich Belin came in to finish it out- he threw for 40 yards on 3-5 passing. Nelson has yet to play a full game for the Orange. He has always exited games due to injury in the three games that he saw significant action. The Boston College game was the first one that Nelson was available for since the North Carolina game. Nelson missed the previous four games as he was recovering from tight-rope surgery to fix a high-ankle sprain. Nelson was the third-string quarterback before the season started. (Photo by Sebastian El-Saqqa - firo sportphoto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich board member for sport Max Eberl has dampened expectations of immediate transfer activity in t he January window, insisting the German record champions will not rush into the market despite a sudden wave of injuries depleting Vincent Kompany’s squad. Speaking to Sky, captured by @iMiaSanMia , following a turbulent weekend that saw both Harry Kane and Michael Olise forced of f during Bayern’s 1-1 Bundesliga draw against 1. FC Köln, Eberl stressed that the club’s sporting leadership will evaluate int ernal recovery timelines before committing to any mid-season additions. “We need t o assess the situation calmly. How are the guys doing? How are they feeling? We won’t rush i nto anything,” Eberl explained. “We’re not going to blindly say, ‘Okay, now we have to do something.’ If we were to make a move, it would have to make se nse. But whether we actually do so remains to be seen.” Beyond internal evaluations, Eberl pointed to the logistical realities of mid-season recruitmen t as a major hurdle for a club operating at Bayern’s standard. “The January transfer window is m ore difficult because the market is different. Which club is willing to let go of its best player in Januar y?” he noted. “And when we look at FC Bayern, we want players who can make us better, or at least ma tch our current level. That’s not easy.” Eberl’s statement comes at a particularly testing period at Säbener Straße. Even so, Eberl reiterated that Bayern will monitor rehabilit ation progress before making any final decisions: “So we need to take a close look at the squad, wh en the injured players will return and what opportunities might arise on the market. item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - DECEMBER 4: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions shares a moment with Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at Ford Field on December 04, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the Detroit Lions, a six-game winning streak, a high-powered offense, and a defense that’s decidedly turned things around since Week 5 isn’t enough to earn consideration from the media as one of the premier teams in the NFL. Despite being atop the NFC North, the Lions aren’t even the team to beat in their own division . How the Lions continue to fly under the radar on a national level is, on one hand, expected. They can’t outplay their geography. They don’t play in New York or California or Illinois, states home to the three biggest sports media markets in the country. They’re not “America’s Team” or the up-and-comers they were ahead of the 2023 season. The pillars of their team remain unchanged from the beginning of a run that includes three of four seasons where the Lions have started the season 8-2 or better—something the franchise had never done in the 60 seasons prior. No matter what they accomplish, preconceptions plague this team. They’re still led by the same Jared Goff everyone decided was the NFL’s Charlie-in-the-Box—the gatekeeper for the Island of Misfit Toys. Remember Charlie from Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer ? He lives on the Island of Misfit Toys because he’s named “Charlie” instead of “Jack,” believing his name is “all wrong” and that no child would ever want a second-rate Charlie-in-the-Box. So sure, Jared looks and acts just as good as the real thing, but his name isn’t Joe or Josh, the names of quarterbacks everyone else fawns over in MVP discussions. The teams of Joe and Josh are being carried by elite quarterback play, and their teams’ mediocre defenses be damned: they’re in firm control of their respective divisions. As for the Lions defense, that’s what’s going to sink their ship this season, just as it did in 2024 when the team went 15-2 and lost to the Washington Commanders in the Divisional Round. According to the pundits, this defense is still the same turnstile it was during the first month of the season, except now its without two of their top defenders in Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson— how could Detroit possibly be considered a top-10 team? In fact, their defensive core will not play a single game together this season, so consider their Super Bowl window shattered . Mind you, we all live in our own echo chambers, seeds planted on a screen where our algorithms grow around us into any shape we encourage it to take: it’s an environment as real as the world. item.title: Fresno State bowl eligible, will face Oregon St in finale
item.description: SAN MARCOS, TX - NOVEMBER 14: Fresno State Bulldogs head coach Matt Entz congratulates players on a scoring play during game featuring the Fresno State Bulldogs and the Texas State Bobcats on November 14, 2026 at UFCU Stadium in San Marcos, TX. (Photo by John Rivera/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Over the weekend the Fresno State Bulldogs got two huge pieces of news. First, they are bowl eligible for the second time in as many years under Matt Entz. Secondly, they know who their opponent will be for the flex schedule this Saturday night as the regular season comes to a close. This past Saturday saw a shootout in the Valley between the Bulldogs and the Colorado State Rams. Jayden Mandel threw three touchdowns, while Speedy Luke ran for two more in the Bulldogs’ 49-42 win over Colorado State to end a two-game losing streak, and knock out the all important sixth win in order to become bowl eligible. Fresno State racked up 265 yards on the ground, with Bryson Donelson going for 165 yards and a touchdown himself. The aforementioned Luke had 68 yards on 10 carries to go with his scores. While the offense was high flying, the defense was all over the place. Beginning with a Simeon Rice 35-yard pick six, it appeared as though Fresno State’s problems on defense were going to be solved. However, that was not the case, as the defense couldn’t stop a nosebleed on Saturday night. Nonetheless, it goes down as a win, the sixth of the season with one contest remaining. The Pac-12 at the beginning of the season had left the final week of the regular season open as a flex scheduled game. Many predicted that the Bulldogs would take on San Diego State. However, with the Aztecs’ stunner in Boise, that game fell into doubt. On Sunday it was announced that the Bulldogs’ final contest of the 2026 regular season will be a rematch of the Halloween night matchup with Oregon State. The Bulldogs took care of business in that first contest, winning 38-22. This next game, like the previous one, will be played in Fresno as it will be Senior Night for the 2026 football team. Fresno State and Oregon State will kickoff at 7 p.m. Pacific Time on Saturday night and will be broadcasted on The CW.

item.title: Shawn Horcoff Makes Telling Admission About Dylan Larkin Trade Return
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings acquired prospect Michael Hage from the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster trade on Sunday night that sent Dylan Larkin north of the border. Hage has played in 13 games this season for the Michigan Wolverines. He has scored five goals and has recorded 21 assists, along with a plus-15 rating. Shawn Horcoff on why Michael Hage mattered Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff spoke with reporters on Monday about the importance of acquiring a player like Hage in a trade for Larkin. Horcoff said, via Brad Galli, “At the end of the day, the opportunity to acquire a prospect like Michael Hage was hard for us to pass up.” Hage is a 20-year-old centerman and has a lot of potential. Denver defenseman Eric Jamieson (15) passes the puck against Michigan forward Michael Hage (19) during the third period of the Frozen Four semifinal at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on Thursday, April 9, 2026 Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Michael Hage does not have an entry-level deal yet Hage was the No. 21 overall pick in the 2024 NHL Draft by Montreal. He is in the middle of his third season with Michigan, and the Wolverines still have games to play. One of the little concerns about trading for Hage is that he is unsigned . Hage did not sign an entry-level deal with Montreal. Detroit fans are hoping that he is going to sign one with the Red Wings once the 2026-27 college hockey season, which is still underway, comes to an end. He has a chance to be an important part of the Red Wings’ future because he is a centerman with top-six potential . Horcoff’s words make it clear that Hage was a player he wanted to acquire for Larkin. item.title: The Viva El Birdos Podcast – Episode 92: Interview with Brian Walton
item.description: Analyzing the Cardinals’ Off-Season Moves Insights on player decisions and future implications for the team. The off-season is a critical time for any sports team, and the St. Louis Cardinals are certainly no exception. Recent decisions, particularly those made during the non-tender deadline, have sparked discussions among fans and analysts alike. In this week’s episode of the Viva El Birdos Podcast, Jake Wood and Brian Walton dive deep into these moves and their implications for the Cardinals’ future. Non-Tendered Players One of the most significant developments was the non-tendering of Nolan Gorman and Max Rajcic. Brian Walton shares his thoughts: “I think everybody understood that Gorman’s time with the Cardinals needed to come to an end both for him and for the team.” For Gorman, who had nearly 2,000 major league plate appearances without finding his footing, this decision wasn’t unexpected. Walton mentions the potential for Gorman to rejuvenate his career overseas: “Maybe he’s a good guy to go overseas and play in Asia.” As for Rajcic, Walton notes his promising run in Triple-A but ultimately points to a lack of long-term potential at the major league level. Future of the Roster The Cardinals are looking to create flexibility as they move forward. Walton explains that the team’s actions reflect a broader strategy: “They wanted to create another roster opening, and they did that. That gives them more flexibility if they want to be a buyer in Rule Five or sign a free agent.” With significant turnover in the roster over the past few years, including the entire starting lineup from the 2023 season minus Jordan Walker, the Cardinals are in a phase of transformation. Both hosts express curiosity about how this will play out in the upcoming season. Player Development Challenges The conversation shifts to the challenges in player development, particularly regarding past draft picks. Walton and Wood discuss how the organization has struggled to maximize the potential of its players: “I think a lot of the talent that he had brought in, the player development aspect of the organization just was not up to par.” This reflection on the Cardinals’ approach highlights the ongoing challenges the team faces in developing young talent and making strategic decisions based on their performance. Looking Ahead As the off-season continues, the Cardinals are tasked with finding the right balance between protecting promising players and making room for new talent. With the Rule Five draft approaching, Walton emphasizes the importance of making sound decisions: “Act like you assume there’s gonna be a draft. Don’t try to get cute.” This episode provides a thoughtful analysis of the Cardinals’ recent moves and what they might mean for the future. item.title: Dylan Larkin breaks silence after trade to Canadiens
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Dylan Larkin breaks silence after trade to Canadiens appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The stalemate between the Detroit Red Wings and Dylan Larkin has come to an end. On Sunday night, the Red Wings traded Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens. On Monday night, Larkin will make his Canadiens debut against the Los Angeles Kings . As the former Red Wings captain prepares for his Canadiens debut, he is breaking his silence on the trade, per Habs on Reddit. “My dad is Canadian, my wife is Canadian. Montreal is such a great city, it has so much to offer. Myself and my whole support system are so excited for something new,” Larkin said. “To be in a great city like Montreal, where it means so much to put that (Habs) jersey on, with its history and the great players and great teams before.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Larkin was the 15th overall selection of the Red Wings in the 2014 NHL Draft. He made his debut with the Wings in the 2015-16 season, and has spent his entire career in Detroit. Larkin played 818 games with 278 goals and 371 assists with the Red Wings. He wore the number 71 with the Red Wings, but that number is currently worn by Jake Evans in Montreal. Instead, Larkin will be wearing number 89 for the Canadiens. Putting on that jersey is something Larkin is excited about. “I love playing in this building,” Larkin said of playing at the Bell Centre. “(To) put that jersey on for the first time in this building, it means something to me. This has been the most disappointing season of the Ryan Day era in Columbus, but one contingent of online Buckeyes fans, known collectively as the “lunatic fringe,” has called for Day to be fired for the last several seasons. After the Nebraska loss, the de facto leader of the fringe, Meet at Midfield’s Ryan Donnelly, and The Comeback’s own Kevin Harish, laid out why they feel Day needs to be fired on their podcast, High Street Freaks. item.title: In A Season Full Of Disaster, Greg Schiano & Rutgers Gives Fans An Unforgettable Moment
item.description: STATE COLLEGE, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 21: Head coach Greg Schiano of the Rutgers Scarlet Knights claps his hands during the second quarter against the Penn State Nittany Lions at Beaver Stadium on November 21, 2026 in State College, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images This has not been said much recently but Rutgers, Greg Schiano — Take a bow. When Clay Thevenin crossed the goal line with no time left on the clock, a weight lifted off the shoulders of the Scarlet Knights that had been sitting there since 1988. “1988, that’s the last time we did it here,” Schiano said after the game on Saturday. “There’s a lot of history in this building, personally. … It was a lot of thought driving in here last night. I have a lot of special memories here, but I don’t know if any of them are more special than this.” RUTGERS WALKS IT OFF WITH A TWO-POINT CONVERSION! What an end to the game for @RFootball pic.twitter.com/SICRoVJ6Lp — FOX College Football (@CFBONFOX) November 22, 2026 First, let’s not overshadow the final 20 minutes as a whole. Rutgers trailed 24-10 getting the ball back with five minutes left in the third quarter. The Scarlet Knights put together a 19-play drive that ended in an Antwan Raymond touchdown. Fast forward to Penn State’s final possession, Rutgers forced a three-and-out to get the ball back. The offense then went on an 11-play drive to get into scoring position. It ended with the incredible play where Raymond pitched the ball back to Ben Black for the score. “I’m really, really proud of this team, their faith, their belief in what we do,” Schiano said. “It would have been easy to say, ‘this isn’t our year,’ and ‘let’s get to next year.’ But there hasn’t been any of that the whole season.” For Rutgers, this snapped a losing streak against the Nittany Lions that dated back to 1988. What might be more amazing is that Rutgers scored a touchdown in State College for the first time since 1994. Since then, Rutgers had played in that stadium five times and kicked seven field goals. The criticism surrounding Schiano and Rutgers has been very loud, and very well warranted, this season. One thing that has remained consistent is that Schiano claims that he hears the frustrations and that his team was going to beat someone that no one expected. As a four-touchdown underdog, Saturday’s historic win over Penn State falls into that category. And for that, Schiano should take a bow. “It hasn’t always been pretty, and I know the fans, the coaches and the players, and everyone is frustrated,” Schiano said. “But this is a good lesson for our guys, what life is about. It doesn’t always come when you want it. But you’ve got to keep chopping; you’ve got to keep fighting.”

As the Colts look to the future, some of the decisions the team makes will be all about 2027 and beyond, not their chances of winning in 2026. Sunday morning, ESPN's Ian Rapoport reported that Pierce was expected to be shut down for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season. But Stephen Holder of ESPN shared that Shane Steichen has other plans, and Pierce isn't out for the year just yet. Colts HC denies that Alec Pierce is shut down for 2026 season "I know there's reports out there on Alec Pierce being done for the season," Steichen said. "We have not made that determination. He's still going through his rehab process. The only way we'll put him out there is if he's 100%. We gotta be really smart." Pierce's heel injury, which led to his placement on injured reserve before Week 3, has lingered all season long. Week 12 is here, and the Colts haven't shown any signs of Pierce coming back. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
